note: defeq_collapse means the statement's two sides reduce to each other at default transparency. That is a CANDIDATE signal, not a verdict: it fires both on vacuous definitional restatements AND on genuine finite computations, because reduction is how a concrete computation is proved. The discriminator is whether the operands are hand-entered constants or actually computed -- spot-checked, most in this batch are hand-entered tables (jonesAtOne is a table whose torusLink2 entry is marked 'placeholder'; klEigenvalueAtOne and pairCount are two separate `Int := 2`).

batch5_note: Batch 5 (2026-08-27): QOU.Mathlib.PermutationEnumeration, run SOLO -- 73 theorems, 58 collapses (79 %), the highest rate in the sample. TWO findings, and the second is the more important. (1) OPERATIONAL: this module had exceeded every batch budget tried and was recorded as unreachable. It completes alone in well under 2400 s. The constraint was the BATCH, not the module -- a batch shares one elaboration and one heartbeat budget, so a single heavy module starves the rest and the whole command dies. Run heavy modules solo rather than declaring them out of reach. (2) CALIBRATION, and it inverts the natural reading of the collapse rate: 79 % here is ENTIRELY LEGITIMATE. `coxeterLength perm := (univ.filter (fun p => p.1 < p.2 and perm p.1 > perm p.2)).card` is the real inversion-count definition over Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm (Fin n)`, so `coxeterLength (s1*s2*s1) = 3 := by decide` enumerates every pair, filters by inversion and counts. It CANNOT be arranged -- a wrong permutation product gives a wrong count. Compare QOU.Mathlib.WenzlBridgeConcrete at 62 %, where the collapses ARE the defect (conjugate-duality lemmas between two defs spelled identically). SO THE COLLAPSE RATE IS NOT A QUALITY SIGNAL, in either direction. The discriminator, stateable now from two measured extremes: does the collapsing computation TRAVERSE A REAL STRUCTURE (a Finset.filter over a permutation group, a Kauffman bracket reduction, a factorial), or does it UNFOLD TWO DEFS THAT WERE SPELLED IDENTICALLY? The first is a computation; the second is a restatement. Note that `local_only` does not separate them either -- the coxeterLength_* group is local_only and legitimate, while permutationCount_n_five is FOREIGN and equally legitimate. What separates them is what the local def DOES.

coverage.note: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-30 for batch 8. QUOTE THIS BLOCK, NOT A BARE MODULE COUNT. The kernel pass has seen 51 of 2257 QOU modules -- 2.3 % of the tree, 3.4 % of what currently has an olean. It is a SAMPLE and the file name says so; nothing here supports a corpus-wide claim about how common defeq collapse is. CORRECTION: PR #5875's scope section said "8 modules still lack oleans". That 8 was scoped to the modules carrying UNADJUDICATED MAJOR FINDINGS at that moment, not to the corpus -- the real figure is 741 of 2257, a third of the Lean tree. Reported as a corpus number it invites the reading that coverage is nearly complete when it is 2.3 %. Same error class as the precision-figure correction one commit earlier (a filtered count published as an unfiltered one), made twice in one session by the agent auditing the corpus for it. The 741 are not all failures: most have simply never been asked for. Two are known compile failures at a 420 s budget (QOU.BraidKnot.JHopfQOneProvenance, QOU.BraidKnot.JonesNuclearQuotient); the rest are untried. scripts/lean/compile-cone.sh reaches any of them without letting `lake build` evict the restored Mathlib cache. RE-MEASURED the same day, and the olean figure had already moved: 741 without an olean (33 %) at 12:5x, 102 (4 %) at 13:3x. CAUSE: `scripts/lean-build-bg.sh`, the SessionStart hook, runs `lake build` in the background for the whole session and had been quietly building the tree the entire time -- QOU oleans 978 -> 2155. So OLEAN COVERAGE IS A MOVING TARGET IN A LIVE SESSION: measure it at the moment of use, never quote it from an earlier run in the same session. Worth recording that the eviction hazard did NOT fire: AGENTS.md and bean qou-r13s warn that a `lake build` against a restored tree drops root mathlib oleans 6990 -> 334. Measured here with that build running for two hours: mathlib is still 6990, untouched, and .lake/RESTORED-NO-TRACES is still present. The qou-r13s scenario is `lake build QOU UGB Fred2005` at the ROOT workspace; this hook builds in the per-paper workspace and adds QOU oleans without rebuilding mathlib. The warning is not wrong -- it is narrower than a blanket 'never let lake build run'. Note the two percentages move in OPPOSITE directions as the tree builds: coverage-of-tree is unchanged at 2.3 % (the numerator and 2257 are both fixed), while coverage-of-olean-reachable FELL from 3.4 % to 2.5 % because its denominator grew. Both are honest; quote the one whose denominator you mean.

batch8_note:
Batch 8 (2026-08-30): 10 modules, 117 theorems, ONE collapse -- 0.85 %, against 25 % accumulated, the lowest rate of any batch by an order of magnitude. That is not a clean bill for these modules; it is the TARGETING telling us something about the pass itself, and it is the most useful thing this batch produced.

TARGETING: these 10 were selected as modules carrying an adjudicated GENUINE verdict in the vacuity ledger, to test whether the kernel pass independently corroborates the text pass. Seven of those verdicts are category `proof-no-self-assuming-projection`.

RESULT: of the 7, the pass SAW 5 and collapsed ZERO. (The other 2 it cannot see at all: `toffoli_transfer_matrix` is a `def` and `TransferMatrixEigenphase` is a `class`, and the pass enumerates theorems.) The single collapse, `QOU.kahler_differentials_no_sym_component`, is not one of the targets.

THE CALIBRATION, and it is STRUCTURAL rather than a sample fluctuation: `defeq_collapse` and `proof-no-self-assuming-projection` are DISJOINT BY CONSTRUCTION. `defeq_collapse` asks whether the STATEMENT's two sides reduce to each other. A self-assuming projection's statement has two opaque class-field applications on either side -- `s.total` versus `s.smooth + s.oscillating` -- and nothing reduces, because a class field is an opaque constant. The defect lives entirely in the PROOF TERM (`s.split_identity`, `ctx.claim_ii_generator_crossing_traced`, `inst.forms_agree`), which this pass does not inspect. So the kernel pass is looking at the wrong half of the declaration for that family, and no amount of added coverage will change that.

WHAT IT DOES CORROBORATE: the OTHER genuine family, `rfl`-against-a-def-arm, where the statement genuinely does collapse. Measured over the previously-scanned modules, ledger entries there split 17 collapse / 2 not among `genuine` verdicts. So read the two together: 17/19 on the def-arm family, 0/5 on the projection family.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PASS, the actionable one: the projection family is the LARGEST in the ledger (111 of 168 genuine verdicts) and is currently text-only. A kernel-level check for it is a DIFFERENT predicate -- is the proof term a bare projection of an instance binder, `.mk` field access with no elimination? -- and is cheap, since it reads the value's head symbol rather than running `isDefEq`. Adding it would give the biggest defect family a machine check for the first time. Also worth fixing: the pass enumerates theorems only, so a `def` carrying a proposition -- the AGENTS.md 1a def-disguise, which is the whole reason that rule exists -- is invisible to it. Both are follow-ups, not done here.

PER-MODULE, so the total is not read as a trend: ChannelSeparation 1/8; all nine others 0 -- GradedTraceResidueSplit 0/6, Information.toffoli_transfer_matrix 0/3, QGeometricLanglands 0/31, Archimedean.MassTowerOpenProblemsClasses 0/15, Mass.CoordinationBinding 0/11, QBeta.EigenphaseCarrierVacuity 0/12, FluidDynamics.q_ns_wellposedness 0/16, Mathlib.SDPDuality 0/7, BraidKnot.WLambdaDefectClosedForm 0/8.

Eviction check after the run: root Mathlib oleans still 6990, `.lake/RESTORED-NO-TRACES` still present. Two 5-module batches run concurrently; both exit 0 in ~9 min wall.
batch9_note:
Batch 9 (2026-08-30): the follow-up batch 8 identified, IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED. `BorrowedNameKernel.valueOnlyProjects` is a second kernel predicate, reported as `value_only_projects`: every constant the PROOF TERM uses from its own module is a structure/class field projection (or the structure itself), and at least one is. So the proof reads its conclusion off its own hypotheses and derives nothing from any other declaration in the file -- the AGENTS.md 3b-cond rule-5 shape, which `defeqCollapse` is structurally unable to see because that defect lives in the value, not the statement.

MEASURED on the SAME 117 theorems batch 8 ran, so the two are directly comparable:
  defeq_collapse         1 / 117   (0.85 %)
  value_only_projects   21 / 117   (17.9 %)
21x more productive on the population where the ledger says the defects are.

RECALL: 6 of 6 targeted findings fire -- graded_trace_residue_split, adjoint_vanishing_propagation, binding_eq_bond_energy, brane_tower_finite, term7_structural (all `genuine`, projection category) and langlands_eigenvalue_swap (`genuine`, borrowed-name, and a projection too). Every one of them has defeq_collapse = false, which is the batch-8 blindness restated from the other side.

PRECISION, on the one case that can actually decide it: `q_ns_wellposedness` does NOT fire. That declaration was `ctx.wellposedness_holds` -- one projection of the whole conclusion, adjudicated `genuine` -- and was remediated to compose two honestly-assumed hypotheses with two conjuncts proved in-file. The predicate separates the pre- and post-remediation forms of the SAME declaration, i.e. it distinguishes the 3b-cond FORBIDDEN pattern from the SANCTIONED one. That is the strongest validation available short of a labelled corpus. `traceInner_nonneg_of_posSemidef` (also remediated) and `twoM_content_decomposition` (a genuine ring identity) likewise do not fire.

KNOWN FALSE-POSITIVE CLASS, named rather than hedged: the predicate looks only at constants from the DECLARATION'S OWN MODULE, so a proof doing real work entirely through MATHLIB is indistinguishable from a pure projection. Two measured instances in this run: `langlands_dual_pos` fires, but its proof is `rw [ld.substrate_inverted]; exact inv_pos.mpr (ld.gaugeGroup.field_pos p)` -- `inv_pos` is real content and is Mathlib, hence invisible here; and `q_ns_energy_inequality` / `q_ns_spectral_decay` fire, and those are precisely the two legitimate conditional derivations the q_ns remediation composed. So a conditional theorem discharging honestly from a stated hypothesis looks the same from here, exactly as the docstring warns. FOLLOW-UP (not done; it would need its own recall measurement): add a count of non-local, non-PACKAGING constants -- excluding And.intro, Iff.intro, Eq.mpr and friends -- and require it to be zero. That would exclude both instances above.

TRAP worth carrying forward, because the FIRST version of this predicate reported ZERO fires across five modules chosen for containing the defect, and read like a clean corpus. Field access on an instance leaves BOTH the projection AND THE STRUCTURE ITSELF in `getUsedConstants`: `s.split_identity` gives `[CommRing, GradedTraceResidueSplit, GradedTraceResidueSplit.split_identity]`. So `ls.all isFieldProjection` is false whenever the structure is local -- which is every case this predicate exists for. Diagnosed by dumping `getUsedConstants` on three known positives rather than by reasoning about it. A detector returning zero on its own designed-for population is a bug until proved otherwise.

STILL INVISIBLE, unchanged from batch 8: the pass enumerates THEOREMS, so a `def` carrying a proposition -- the AGENTS.md 1a def-disguise -- is not examined. `toffoli_transfer_matrix` is one, adjudicated `genuine`, and its module reports 0 of 3.
batch10_note:
Batch 10 (2026-08-30): the SECOND follow-up batch 8 named -- the pass now analyses a `def` whose TYPE IS A PROP, not theorems only. That is the AGENTS.md 1a def-disguise, and a theorem-only pass was blind to exactly the shape that rule exists to forbid: `theorem X : True := trivial` becomes invisible to every vacuity detector the moment it is re-declared as a `def`, which is why 1a names the move.

RESULT, and the exclusions are why it is a scalpel rather than a flood: across five re-run modules the declaration count rose by exactly ONE, and that one is `QOU.Information.toffoli_transfer_matrix` -- adjudicated `genuine` in the ledger, a `def`, and previously reported by its own module as 0 of 3 analysable declarations, i.e. the kernel pass could not see the finding at all. It now fires `value_only_projects = true`. The two exclusions in `isAuthoredClaim` are load-bearing: a Prop-valued CLASS FIELD is a `DefnInfo` with a Prop type, and an INSTANCE asserts inhabitation; admitting either would add every hypothesis field of every class in the module, which are declarations of an assumption rather than claims about it (and instance honesty is the 3b-tax conjecture-carrier question, a different audit).

STILL invisible, correctly: a `class` carrier such as `TransferMatrixEigenphase` -- EigenphaseCarrierVacuity stayed at 12 declarations. Same reason.

### CORRECTION -- the '17 collapse / 2 not' figure was WRONG, twice over

PR #6093's body and the batch-8 commit both said the genuine verdicts in scanned modules split '17 collapse / 2 not' on the def-arm family. **Do not quote that.** Two independent defects, and the first is the one worth internalising.

1. METHOD. The cross-tab matched a ledger entry to a kernel finding by BARE DECLARATION NAME. Names repeat across files -- the ledger holds `strong_duality` twice (`MathlibExt/SDP.lean` and `mass-theory/confinement-nf-partial-proof.lean`) and the kernel had scanned a THIRD, unadjudicated `QOU.Mathlib.SDPDuality.strong_duality` with eight real hypotheses and a genuine proof. So a decl name got credited with any collapse anywhere. This is the arity/identity conflation AGENTS.md 'Grep the claim SHAPE' warns about, committed in the tooling that measures the audit that exists to catch it. Key by MODULE + DECL.
2. READING. Even under the wrong method the same run reported 9 non-collapsing genuine entries, not 2. The '2' does not appear in any output.

MEASURED CORRECTLY, keyed by module + decl, genuine entries in scanned modules:
  proof-borrowed-name                12 / 18   (67 %)  -- the def-arm / decide family
  proof-no-self-assuming-projection   0 /  7
  proof-zero-placeholder              0 /  1
  TOTAL                              12 / 26   (46 %)

THE CONCLUSION IS UNCHANGED AND BETTER SUPPORTED. The blindness on the projection family is now 0 of 7 rather than 0 of 5 -- complete, and on one more case than before, because `toffoli_transfer_matrix` is finally visible to be counted. What moved is the def-arm figure: 67 %, not 89 %. Read the SPLIT BY FAMILY, never the total; the crude 17/19 was an artifact of a broken join and the 46 % total mixes two families whose rates are 67 % and 0 %.
